name: Level Slider
blurb: A range whose stops have names - effort, size, density, any short ordered scale.
mechanism: A native `<input type=range>` with `step=1`, plus a label per stop placed at its exact fraction of the track. Because it is a real range, arrow keys, Home/End and PageUp/PageDown all work and it announces as a slider - none of which is written here.
caveats: The active stop is highlighted from a `data-v` attribute the inline `oninput` writes, because CSS cannot read an input's value. One rule per stop; fine for a control whose whole premise is few named stops.
The stop labels are `aria-hidden`: the input already announces its value, and reading the scale twice is worse than reading it once. Give the input an `aria-label` that names what is being chosen.
Six stops is about the limit before the labels collide on a narrow track. Past that, this is a select.
support: `clip-path` on a range thumb for the pole variant - a thumb cannot host a pseudo-element, so the marker shape has to be cut out of the thumb itself.
